text: English practice: The submitted abstract proposes Anchor Switching. It treats several dental arch models as independent tracking targets and transfers the pose from the most stable target to an output model. The goal is to maintain AR implant guidance when part of the cast is occluded. The submitted experiment used left and right segmented arch models.

text: English practice: Since submission, the implementation has changed in four ways. We replaced the tracking backend with a Python implementation of M3T. We created smaller tooth-region models and a smooth combined arch. We corrected the physical model scale using an ArUco reference. We also updated the camera calibration and the Unity coordinate conversion for the 720p setup.

text: English practice: I added a quality-based recovery strategy. A short degradation does not immediately trigger a global search. Instead, the system holds the last reliable pose while continuing to test the current image. If the low-quality state continues, it starts a guarded relock and later expands the search if necessary. We still need systematic measurements under the final demo setup.

text: For the progress meeting: this is the central decision. The submitted contribution is dynamic anchor selection. The current default configuration prioritizes stability by using one combined rigid body. If the conference demonstration must visually show switching, set SINGLE_BODY_MODE to false and verify the four independent anchors. If the single-body mode is used, describe it as a post-submission implementation update and do not claim that A-D highlighting is actual switching.

Our submitted demonstration addresses tracking loss caused by partial occlusion during AR-assisted dental implant treatment. The abstract describes Anchor Switching, which selects the most stable pose from multiple dental arch models and transfers it to the AR output. Since submission, we replaced the original tracking backend with a Python implementation of M3T and investigated tooth-region models that avoid the artificial cut surfaces of the earlier left-right segmentation. For the current stable configuration, we combine the visible tooth groups into one rigid-body model. This is an implementation update rather than anchor switching. We also corrected the physical scale, updated the 720p camera calibration, and added quality-based pose holding and relocking. I will demonstrate the current tracking behavior and explain how these changes relate to the submitted method.
